dod_intent_evidence: Their own newsroom: 'Hydrosat Secures $1.9 Million Contract from the US Air Force to Enhance Thermal Imagery for National Defense' (2024-10-16) and 'Hydrosat Awarded Stage II Contract by NRO' (2025-07-21), backed by an Air Force 2022 SBIR Phase II ($1,200,000) and a USAspending record (FA864922P0959).
score_evidence: 'Our next-generation constellation ... will deliver daily, continuous monitoring of any location, combining 25 m high-resolution thermal imagery with coincident 10 m visible data. This unmatched commercial capability...' → lab_language_intensity: the differentiating capability is future tense and pitched in resolution/swath specs

'Hydrosat's systems have flight-heritage and are engineered to meet standards for civil and national security missions.' → deployment_awareness_absence: 'standards' is never named — across ~1382 words there is no ATO/RMF, IL5/IL6, ITAR, export control, CMMC, or classified-dissemination language
'Insights are available through a web portal, mobile application, and API.' → deployment_awareness_absence: the entire delivery model assumes an internet-connected commercial user

Audience is consistently civil/commercial — 'policymakers, irrigation districts, and farms' and 'decision makers across the world' — with 'analysts can tip higher-resolution sensors to the right location' the only nod to an operational user; no warfighter, CONOPS, training, or field-feedback language → operator_absence

Open roles include 'Capture Manager – U.S. Government Contracts' (three postings), 'Senior Security Engineer' (two postings), and 'Test Engineer' → hiring_profile_skew scored low: they are visibly staffing government capture, security, and test rather than researchers only

106 employees, two satellites on orbit (VZ-1, VZ-2, 2025), '$20 Million in Investment and Grants' (2023), recurring ag subscription revenue → stage_pressure low; the pressure is constellation capex, not a period-of-performance cliff

blind_spots.blind_spot: The engineering organization is distributed across Luxembourg and Berlin while the customers are NRO and the Air Force
blind_spots.operator_reality: Thermal collection specifications, calibration data, and tasking parameters for a system the NRO is assessing on orbit sit squarely in export-controlled territory. Their own open roles put 'Platform Engineer' in Berlin and 'Operations & HR Manager' in Luxembourg on the same pipeline that produces the national-security product. ITAR/EAR and foreign-person access controls do not surface at contract award — they surface at the accreditation and data-handling review, by which point the build path has to be split and re-staffed, and that rework is measured in quarters against a running period of performance.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The company grew its engineering base around the European agriculture business (the IrriWatch acquisition, Luxembourg HQ presence), and the defense line was added on top of an already-international org rather than architected separately.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Delivery is a commercial web portal and API, with no described route onto the networks the intelligence customer actually works on
blind_spots.operator_reality: An NRO or Air Force analyst consuming thermal tips does that work on a classified enclave. Every insight therefore has to cross a domain boundary — accreditation, a cross-domain solution, or a government-hosted instance at IL5/IL6. Their described product ships 'daily alerts, maps, and actionable guidance' to a browser and a mobile app. The gap between 'we deliver via API' and 'the analyst can see it at their desk' is the months-to-field number that kills transitions.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The delivery architecture was built for irrigation districts and growers, where a web portal and a phone app are exactly right, and the same stack is being pointed at a defense customer without re-examining where the user sits.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Real-time data with daily alerts, maps, and actionable guidance

blind_spots.blind_spot: The value proposition is calibrated to agricultural time, not operational time
blind_spots.operator_reality: '2+ Weeks earlier risk detection' and 'Thermal anomalies often emerge weeks before changes become visible' is a compelling claim for drought and crop stress. A tip-and-cue role in a defense architecture is judged on latency from collection to a usable cue — hours, sometimes minutes — plus revisit over a specific area of interest and a defined timeliness SLA. Daily continuous revisit is explicitly the next-generation constellation, not what is on orbit today, so the defense capability being sold and the capability that exists are separated by a launch campaign.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Their entire proof base — '60+ countries served', 'Proven across 220k+ acres', 'Solutions used daily on millions of hectares' — is agricultural, where a two-week lead time is the headline benefit, so no internal metric measures cue latency.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Thermal anomalies often emerge weeks before changes become visible to the human eye or traditional sensors.

opener_hook: Hydrosat's NRO Stage II award covers on-orbit assessment of its infrared data, and its platform engineering roles are posted in Berlin and Luxembourg — the export-control question that usually surfaces at accreditation rather than at award.
what_they_do: Builds and flies thermal-infrared imaging satellites and sells the surface-temperature data and analytics, mostly for agriculture and water management, with a growing national-security line for thermal anomaly detection.
